text: The implementation of the new library scheme facilitated a substantial improvement in access to reading materials. Students who previously encountered difficulties obtaining appropriate resources were able to participate more frequently in classroom discussions. Furthermore, the initiative demonstrated the importance of providing assistance to families who could not afford additional books. The teachers observed that attendance improved after the scheme began. However, they acknowledged that the available evidence was insufficient to establish whether the books alone caused this change. A number of parents also reported that their children were spending more time reading at home. The school will continue to collect feedback before deciding whether to expand the scheme next year.

The school consequently agreed to review the timetable, taking into account both the teachers' observations and the students' accounts of their experiences, before introducing any further changes.

The writer calls the sea a “fierce breaker” and describes the surfers as being “on the verge of engulfment.” This illustrates the danger they face. The strong language makes the waves seem powerful and gives the reader a sense of fear. Later, the surfers are described as having “waded quietly ashore.” That contrast helps the reader understand how quickly the mood changes from danger to safety. The quoted words must stay exactly as written because they are evidence from the passage.

Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy. Chlorophyll absorbs light, and the plant uses that energy to produce sugars from carbon dioxide and water. The experiment demonstrates that light intensity can affect the rate of photosynthesis. However, temperature and carbon dioxide availability also matter. These factors were held constant during the experiment so the students could compare the effect of light alone. The results do not show that increasing light always increases growth, because other factors can limit the process.

These samples were not identical, so the results cannot establish a direct change in individual behaviour. Further details are available at https://example.org/research. Their teacher have already booked the tickets and arranged the groups. Some students forgot to bring their lunch, but there was enough food to share. Everyone enjoyed the visit and learned something about the town.

The garden made a significant difference to the neighbourhood. People began to spend more time outside and talk to neighbours they had barely met before. The first few weeks were difficult because the ground was dry and many plants needed extra care.

Furthermore, the garden gave children a place to learn how food grows. They planted beans and watched the leaves appear. Some plants did not survive, but the children learned from those failures.

The project depended on volunteers. Without their regular help, the garden would have been difficult to maintain. The group plans to meet again next spring.

Mary Jones and David Brown visited New Zealand during the school holidays. They used a well-known walking route near Wellington and carried a first-aid kit. When the weather changed, they asked for assistance at the visitor centre. The guide explained that the longer route was closed after heavy rain. They did not continue along that route. Instead, they followed the shorter path back to town and returned before dark.

The first experiment did not show that the treatment worked. The researchers had insufficient evidence to make that claim, even though some participants said they felt better. They consequently planned a second study with a larger group. The second study has not started yet, so its results cannot be compared with the first. Neither the researchers nor the participants know whether the treatment will succeed. The report describes uncertainty rather than a confirmed benefit.
